I'd like to go through each area — can we start with SRE's findings on the queue-worker deployment and what triggered the duplication?

transcript.text: I'd like to share something significant that I found while tracing the worker deployment during a separate code review. There's an undocumented retry shortcut in the worker code that bypasses the webhook idempotency key on the second attempt. I confirmed this behavior only shortly before this review, which is why I haven't filed the remediation ticket yet — but I believe this is likely the root cause of the duplicate deliveries we saw on Tuesday. The retry shortcut means that when the worker retries a failed webhook delivery, it doesn't check the idempotency key, so the same payload can be delivered twice to a customer without being deduplicated. I'll be filing the remediation ticket immediately after this meeting.

transcript.text: Thanks everyone. I appreciate the floor. While checking an unrelated alert migration, I discovered that the duplicate-delivery alert has been disabled for ten days. Additionally, the correct alert threshold for this service is 15 minutes — but the incident lasted 26 minutes, meaning even if the alert had been enabled, it should have fired before the 26-minute mark. I have not yet updated the monitoring ticket with this information, and I want to make sure the group is aware before we finalize the remediation register. I'll be updating that ticket immediately after this meeting as well.
